risks.description: Broadening existing bridge checks for convenience could make legacy bridge inputs less strict.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit product mode with legacy default unchanged and tests proving rejection of invalid product inputs.

risks.description: Pipeline prereg approval and legacy bridge approval have different actors, scopes, and hash binding semantics.
risks.mitigation: Require a bridge-specific Karl exact-content approval marker for product bridge preparation.

risks.description: Instantiating bridge under a fake legacy WP would hide product authority from ToolContext.
risks.mitigation: Add explicit product-mode ToolContext allowlist and reject fake or unsupported WP IDs.

risks.description: Moving product source or output artifacts into legacy prefixes would bypass package-local product evidence discipline.
risks.mitigation: Validate product source and output paths against the active product package scratch root.

risks.description: Current unblocked bridge path invokes the offline runner, which is forbidden for the product bridge-preparation stage.
risks.mitigation: Expose preparation-only product mode that cannot call runner and tests that runner permissions are not used.

risks.description: Product-side reimplementation can diverge from bridge validation, derived artifacts, and denominator semantics.
risks.mitigation: Reject reimplementation; bridge module must remain owner of bridge output generation.

risks.description: Bridge-shaped packets emitted outside bridge validation could appear authoritative without the real checks.
risks.mitigation: Forbid adapter-side fabricated bridge outputs and require bridge-owned validation and write path.

risks.description: Bridge product mode could accidentally imply canonical evidence, candidate lifecycle, promotion/readiness, or runtime authority.
risks.mitigation: Keep explicit false flags, non-authority assertions, no canonical writes, no candidate lifecycle, and no paper/live/runtime contact.
